Definition: as if dative case of κύκλος (a ring, "cycle"; akin to G2947); i.e. in a circle (by implication, of G1722), i.e. (adverbially) all around:--round about.
BiblicalUsage: Round about is the plain adverb for what surrounds, and it does its work in two kinds of scenes. In Mark 3:34 Jesus looks round about on those sitting around Him and says, "Behold my mother and my brethren," and in Luke 9:12 the disciples ask Him to send the multitude into the towns and country round about.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the word is a small reminder of where Jesus stood: in the middle of the circle, with His people around Him, and that is still where He is.
